proof.text: Put $L=u^s$ and $R=g_*$. The hypotheses (a),(b) of [def-weil-pbc-special-cocontinuous-functor] give cocontinuity and continuity. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-continuous-cocontinuous-topos-adjunction] to these small sites. Thus $g^{-1}=L$ is restriction, $R\mathcal F(V)$ consists of the compatible families specified there, the counit is evaluation at $(U,\mathrm{id})$, and the unit sends $t$ to its restrictions along all $\psi:u(A)\to V$. We prove these two maps bijective; the remaining hypotheses (c),(d),(e) enter below.

proof.text: Fix a sheaf $\mathcal F$ on $\mathcal C$, $U\in\mathcal C$ and $s\in\mathcal F(U)$. Given $\psi:u(A)\to u(U)$, choose by (d) a covering $\{f_i:A_i\to A\}$ and arrows $c_i:A_i\to U$ with $u(c_i)=\psi u(f_i)$. On $P=A_i\times_A A_j$, continuity identifies $u(P)$ with $u(A_i)\times_{u(A)}u(A_j)$, so $u(c_i\operatorname{pr}_1)=u(c_j\operatorname{pr}_2)$. By (c) these two arrows become equal on a covering of $P$. Consequently the restrictions of $c_i^*s$ and $c_j^*s$ agree on that covering and hence on $P$, by the injectivity part of the sheaf equalizer condition. Its existence part gives a unique section $t_{A,\psi}\in\mathcal F(A)$ restricting to $c_i^*s$. All fibre products invoked exist by the covering-base-change site axiom. The section is independent of the chosen covering and lifts: on the common refinement $A_i\times_A A'_j$, the two lifts to $U$ have equal $u$-images by continuity, so (c) and separatedness identify their pullbacks of $s$; separatedness on the refinement identifies the two glued sections.

source.place: Tag 03A0 (lemma-equivalence), counit surjectivity paragraph and overlap diagram

proof.text: For $a:B\to A$, pull the chosen covering of $A$ back to $B$. Its arrows $q_i:B\times_A A_i\to B$ and maps $c_i\operatorname{pr}_2:B\times_A A_i\to U$ are lifts of $\psi u(a)$, because $a q_i=f_i\operatorname{pr}_2$. By independence of choices from step 2, $t_{B,\psi u(a)}=a^*t_{A,\psi}$. Therefore the $t_{A,\psi}$ form an element of $R\mathcal F(u(U))$. Choosing the identity covering and identity lift for $(U,\mathrm{id})$ gives $t_{U,\mathrm{id}}=s$. Conversely, any compatible family with this value has $f_i^*s_{A,\psi}=c_i^*s$ by compatibility with the arrows from $(A_i,u(c_i))$ to both $(A,\psi)$ and $(U,\mathrm{id})$. Sheaf separatedness forces $s_{A,\psi}=t_{A,\psi}$. Evaluation is thus bijective, proving the counit $LR\mathcal F\to\mathcal F$ is an isomorphism. This uses only evaluation, not the incorrect assertion in the source that $(U,\mathrm{id})$ is final.

proof.text: For a sheaf $\mathcal G$ on $\mathcal D$ and any $U$, the composite of the unit component $\eta_{\mathcal G,u(U)}:\mathcal G(u(U))\to RL\mathcal G(u(U))$ with the counit evaluation $RL\mathcal G(u(U))\to\mathcal G(u(U))$ is the identity: the $(U,\mathrm{id})$ coordinate of the unit family is $\mathrm{id}^*t=t$. Step 3 says evaluation is bijective, so $\eta_{\mathcal G,u(U)}$ is its inverse, hence bijective.

Write $H=RL\mathcal G$, a sheaf by step 1. For any $V$, choose by (e) a covering $\{v_i:u(U_i)\to V\}$. If two sections of $\mathcal G(V)$ have the same image under $\eta_V$, their restrictions to $u(U_i)$ agree by step 4 and naturality; separatedness gives equality on $V$. Here $V$ was arbitrary, so this proves $\eta_W$ injective for every object $W$. Given $h\in H(V)$, step 4 supplies unique $t_i\in\mathcal G(u(U_i))$ mapping to $h|_{u(U_i)}$. On $u(U_i)\times_Vu(U_j)$ their restrictions have the same image by naturality; the just-proved injectivity on that object implies equality. The sheaf condition glues them to $t\in\mathcal G(V)$. The sections $\eta_V(t)$ and $h$ agree on the covering and hence agree by separatedness of $H$. Thus $\eta_V$ is surjective as well as injective. This fills the source's 'we see easily' without assuming overlaps themselves lie in the image of $u$. Empty coverings cause no exception: the equalizer condition forces singleton section sets on any object with an empty covering.

proof.text: The unit $\mathrm{id}_{\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal D)}\to RL$ and counit $LR\to\mathrm{id}_{\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C)}$ are natural transformations by the adjunction, and their components are bijections by steps 3 and 5. Their componentwise inverses are natural: the naturality square is rearranged by composing with the inverse components. Hence $L$ and $R$ are quasi-inverse equivalences, with these natural isomorphisms as the equivalence data. Since step 1 identifies $L$ with the inverse image of the associated morphism of topoi, that morphism is an equivalence and its inverse image is precisely precomposition with $u$.

title: Special cocontinuous restriction preserves sheaves
statement: Let $\mathcal C,\mathcal D$ be small sites [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] and $u:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ a special cocontinuous functor, meaning that it is cocontinuous, continuous, locally faithful, locally full, and cover-dense with precisely the covering conditions of [def-weil-pbc-special-cocontinuous-functor]. Then the associated morphism of topoi $g:\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C)\to\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal D)$ is an equivalence. Its inverse-image functor is precomposition with $u$, so precomposition is an equivalence between the categories of sheaves of sets on $\mathcal D$ and $\mathcal C$.
